examples.en: If you put crown daisy in the stew, it smells nice.
Crown daisy has a strong scent, so people either love or hate it.
I bought a bunch of crown daisy at the market.
I blanched the crown daisy lightly and seasoned it.
Fish cake soup feels lacking without crown daisy.
I eat crown daisy and lettuce together as a wrap.

explain: 이름에 '쑥'이 들어가지만 쑥과는 다른 채소예요. 탕, 찌개, 쌈에 향을 더하려고 넣는 경우가 많아요. 받침 ㅅ이 [ㄷ]으로 소리 나서 발음은 [쑥깓]이에요.

phrases.en: The crown daisy scent is strong, so the soup tastes refreshing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 채소의 독특한 냄새를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for the vegetable's distinctive aroma.

phrases.en: I put crown daisy on top of the hot pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마지막에 향을 더하려고 얹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when adding it on top at the end for aroma.
phrases.en_equiv: to put crown daisy on top

phrases.en: I trimmed the crown daisy to prepare dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹기 전에 다듬고 손질하는 과정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes cleaning and trimming it before eating.

explain_en: Although it has '쑥' in its name, it is a different vegetable from mugwort. It is often added to soups, stews and wraps for aroma. The final ㅅ sounds like ㄷ, so it is pronounced [쑥깓].

examples.en: This summer the cherries in the yard ripened to a bright red.
I bought a bag of cherries at the market.
The baby's lips are small and red like cherries.

examples.ko: 앵두 철에는 할머니 댁 마당이 붉게 물들어요.
examples.en: In cherry season, my grandmother's yard turns red.
I tried making jam with cherries and it's tangy.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 마당에서 앵두를 따 먹곤 했어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I used to pick and eat cherries in the yard.

explain: 앵두는 작고 새콤한 빨간 열매예요. 마트에서 파는 크고 달콤한 열매는 보통 '체리'라고 불러서 서로 다르게 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 앵두 같은 입술로 유명해요.
phrases.en: That actress is famous for her cherry-red lips.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작고 붉고 예쁜 입술을 칭찬하는 비유예요. 조금 옛날 느낌이 나는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech praising small, red, pretty lips. It sounds a bit old-fashioned.

explain_en: Tiny bright red summer fruit, sweet and tart. 앵두 is a small, tart red fruit. The larger, sweeter fruit sold in supermarkets is usually called '체리', so the two names are used for different fruits.

t90.ax: I bought a bag of cherries at the market.

examples.en: On a cold day I think of mushroom hot pot.
I ate beef hot pot with my family.
When the hot pot boils, add more vegetables.
This restaurant's tripe hot pot is delicious.

examples.ko: 전골 국물에 라면 사리를 넣어 먹었어요.
examples.en: I added instant noodles to the hot pot broth and ate it.

examples.ko: 손님이 오면 전골을 테이블 위에서 끓여요.
examples.en: When guests come, we boil the hot pot on the table.

explain: '전골'은 재료를 담은 냄비를 상 위에서 직접 끓이면서 먹는 요리예요. '찌개'는 주방에서 끓여 내오는 경우가 많은 것과 달라요. 재료가 풍성해서 같이 먹는 사람이 많을 때 시켜요.

phrases.en: I ate seafood hot pot with friends on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 전골 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the main ingredient before it to name the kind of jeongol.

phrases.example: 엄마가 상 위에서 전골을 끓여 주셨어요.
phrases.en: My mother boiled jeongol for us at the table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전골을 만드는 모습을 말할 때 '끓이다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 끓이다 when describing cooking jeongol.
phrases.en_equiv: to boil a hot pot stew

phrases.en: There is a good jeongol restaurant near my office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전골을 파는 식당이에요. '-집'은 음식 이름 뒤에 붙어 그 음식을 파는 가게를 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A restaurant that serves jeongol. The suffix -집 after a food name means a place that sells that food.

explain_en: '전골' is a dish boiled right at the table as you eat, in a pot already filled with ingredients. '찌개' is often brought out already cooked from the kitchen, which is different. It is full of ingredients, so people order it when eating with a group.

examples.en: Milk has a lot of calcium.
Calcium is very good for your bones and teeth.
Anchovies also contain calcium.
If you lack calcium, your bones get weak.
The doctor told me to take calcium pills.
My grandmother gets her calcium from tofu.

explain: '칼슘이 풍부하다', '칼슘이 부족하다'처럼 '풍부하다·부족하다'와 자주 써요. 한국에서는 멸치, 우유, 두부가 칼슘이 많은 음식으로 유명해요. 약국에서 파는 영양제는 '칼슘제'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Anchovies are rich in calcium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칼슘이 많이 들어 있는 음식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for foods that contain a lot of calcium.

phrases.en: If you lack calcium, your bones get weak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 칼슘이 모자랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the body does not get enough calcium.

phrases.en: I bought calcium supplements at the pharmacy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약국에서 파는 칼슘 영양제를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to calcium supplements sold at the pharmacy.

explain_en: It often pairs with '풍부하다' (abundant) and '부족하다' (lacking), as in '칼슘이 풍부하다'. In Korea anchovies, milk and tofu are famous calcium foods. A supplement from a pharmacy is called '칼슘제'.

examples.ko: 저는 탄산이 들어간 음료수를 좋아하지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't like drinks that contain carbonation.
I like drinks with carbonation.
The fizz is gone, so it tastes flat.
Fizzy drinks are bad for your teeth.
I drank sparkling water with lemon.
The carbonation is strong, so my throat stings.

examples.ko: 저는 탄산을 못 마셔서 물을 시켜요.
examples.en: I can't drink fizzy drinks, so I order water.

explain: 원래는 화학 용어지만 일상에서는 콜라나 사이다 속 '톡 쏘는 거품'을 '탄산'이라고 불러요. '탄산음료', '탄산수'처럼 붙여 쓰고, '탄산이 세다/약하다/빠지다'로 정도를 말해요.

phrases.en: Don't drink too many soft drinks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 콜라나 사이다 같은 거품 있는 음료예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fizzy drinks such as cola or lemon-lime soda.

phrases.en: I often drink sparkling water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거품이 있는 물을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to water with bubbles.

phrases.example: 이 사이다는 탄산이 세서 목이 따가워요.
phrases.en: This soda is so fizzy that it stings my throat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거품이 강하다고 정도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the fizz is strong.

explain_en: Originally a chemistry term, in daily life it means the fizz in cola or soda. It joins into words like 탄산음료 and 탄산수, and you describe strength with 탄산이 세다, 약하다, or 빠지다.

en: relieving a hangover; eating a soup or having a drink for a hangover

examples.en: Hot soup is the best way to settle your stomach the next day.
People often eat bean sprout soup to settle the stomach.
The hangover soup restaurant had many customers from the morning.

examples.ko: 속이 안 좋을 때는 해장에 좋은 국물이 생각나요.
examples.en: When my stomach feels bad, I think of soup that's good for settling it.

examples.ko: 해장이 필요할 때는 따뜻한 국을 먹어요.
examples.en: When I need to settle my stomach, I eat a warm soup.

examples.ko: 한국 사람들은 해장을 위해 라면도 먹어요.
examples.en: Koreans also eat ramyeon to settle their stomachs.

explain: '해장국', '해장 라면'처럼 뒤에 음식 이름을 붙이는 경우가 많아요. 과음한 다음 날 속을 풀려고 먹는 따뜻한 국물 음식 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 식당 간판에서도 '해장국'이라는 말을 쉽게 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 어제 많이 마셔서 오늘 해장국을 먹었어요.
phrases.en: I drank a lot yesterday, so I had hangover soup today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해장'이 음식 이름이 된 말로, 속을 풀어 주는 국을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The soup eaten to settle the stomach after drinking.

phrases.en: I really want to eat hangover ramen.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해장' 뒤에 음식 이름을 붙이면 속 풀려고 먹는 음식이라는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a food name after 해장 to mean food eaten for a hangover.

phrases.en: Bean sprout soup is good for a hangover.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 음식이 속을 풀기에 좋다고 할 때 '해장에 좋다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Say this when a food is good for relieving a hangover.

explain_en: It is often followed by a food name, as in '해장국' or '해장 라면'. It comes up in talk about warm, soupy food eaten the day after drinking too much to settle the stomach. You can easily see the word '해장국' on restaurant signs.

examples.ko: 아이들은 관찰력이 좋아서 작은 변화도 알아채요.
examples.en: Kids have sharp observation skills and notice even small changes.

examples.ko: 그 탐정은 뛰어난 관찰력으로 단서를 찾았어요.
examples.en: The detective found clues with his excellent powers of observation.

examples.ko: 그림을 그리면 관찰력을 키울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Drawing can help you build your observation skills.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 관찰력이 없어서 머리 모양이 바뀐 것도 몰라요.
examples.en: My friend isn't observant and doesn't even notice a changed hairstyle.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 관찰력과 집중력을 함께 길러 줘요.
examples.en: This game builds both observation skills and concentration.
For doctors, the ability to observe patients is important.

explain: '관찰력이 좋다/뛰어나다', '관찰력을 기르다'처럼 써요. 보고 금방 따라 하거나 익히는 솜씨는 '눈썰미'라는 말을 따로 써요.

phrases.example: 그림을 그리면 관찰력을 기를 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Drawing can help you build your powers of observation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연습해서 더 잘 보는 힘을 키운다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means growing the ability to observe through practice.

phrases.en: I lack observation skills, so I often miss things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 알아채지 못하는 자신이나 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe someone who doesn't notice things well.

phrases.example: 동생은 눈썰미가 좋아서 요리를 금방 배워요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling has a quick eye, so they learn cooking fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보고 금방 따라 하는 솜씨를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the knack of copying quickly just by watching.
phrases.en_equiv: quick eye; knack for picking up by watching

explain_en: It is used as in '관찰력이 좋다/뛰어나다' and '관찰력을 기르다'. The knack of picking things up quickly just by watching has its own word, '눈썰미'.

en: to be nimble; to be quick

examples.en: Cats are nimble, so they jump high.
That player dodged the ball nimbly.
I like the shoes with the sleek design.
He is big but quick on his feet.

examples.ko: 어제 본 축구 선수는 정말 날렵했어요.
examples.en: The soccer player I saw yesterday was really agile.
The new car's front looks sleek.

explain: '날쌔다'는 움직임이 아주 빠를 때 쓰고, '날렵하다'는 움직임에 더해 몸매나 모양이 군더더기 없이 깔끔할 때까지 써요. 그래서 사람과 동물의 몸 말고도 구두, 자동차 같은 물건의 모양에도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 날렵한 몸으로 빠르게 달려요.
phrases.en: That player runs fast with a nimble body.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 활용으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -ㄴ form modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.en: That cat is really nimble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 지금 모습을 간단히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The 해요 form for simply describing how something is now.

phrases.en: He moved nimbly and caught the ball.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'로 바꿔 동작이 빠르고 깔끔하다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -게 form adds the sense that the movement is quick and neat.

explain_en: '날쌔다' is for very fast movement, while '날렵하다' adds a sense of a lean, clean shape. So it works for bodies and also for the look of things like shoes and cars.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 단결력이 강해서 체육 대회에서 우승했어요.
examples.en: Our class has strong unity, so we won the sports day.

examples.ko: 위기에서 단결력을 보여 준 팀이 결국 이겼어요.
examples.en: The team that showed unity in the crisis won in the end.

examples.ko: 단결력은 말보다 함께 하는 행동에서 생겨요.
examples.en: Unity comes from acting together rather than from words.

examples.ko: 회사 단결력을 키우려고 다 같이 등산을 갔어요.
examples.en: We all went hiking together to build the company's unity.

examples.ko: 단결력이 약한 팀은 오래 가기 어려워요.
examples.en: A team with weak unity has a hard time lasting.

examples.ko: 응원단의 단결력 덕분에 선수들이 힘을 냈어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the cheering squad's unity, the players found strength.

explain: '단결'은 여러 사람이 마음을 하나로 모으는 것이고, '단결력'은 그 힘이에요. '팀워크'와 비슷하지만 '단결력'은 마음을 모으는 면이 더 커요. '강하다/약하다', '키우다', '보여 주다'와 자주 같이 써요.

phrases.en: Our team has strong unity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단결하는 힘이 크다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise a group's strong power of unity.

phrases.en: We built up our unity by exercising together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 활동해서 마음을 모으는 힘을 늘린다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means increasing a group's unity through shared activities.

phrases.en: The classmates united and won.
phrases.nuance_ko: '단결력'의 바탕이 되는 말로, 마음을 하나로 모으는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The base word of '단결력', meaning to come together as one.

explain_en: '단결' means people joining their hearts as one, and '단결력' is the strength of that. It is similar to 'teamwork', but '단결력' stresses the unity of spirit. It often goes with '강하다/약하다', '키우다' and '보여 주다'.

examples.ko: 동생은 손재주가 좋아서 뭐든 잘 만들어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is good with their hands and makes anything well.
Thanks to my mother's handiwork, the house became pretty.

examples.ko: 저는 손재주가 없어서 선물 포장도 서툴러요.
examples.en: I'm not good with my hands, so I'm clumsy even at gift wrapping.
I want to use my manual skill to open a workshop.
My grandfather was a carpenter with outstanding skill.

examples.ko: 손재주 좋은 친구가 가방을 고쳐 줬어요.
examples.en: A friend who is good with their hands fixed my bag.

explain: '손재주가 있다/없다', '좋다/뛰어나다'로 말하고, 말솜씨나 머리가 좋은 것에는 쓰지 않아요. 비슷한 '손끝이 야무지다'는 일을 꼼꼼하고 단정하게 한다는 칭찬이고, 요리 솜씨는 따로 '손맛'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I'm good with my hands, so I'm good at origami.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 하는 일을 잘한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you are good at things done by hand.
phrases.en_equiv: to be good with one's hands

phrases.en: I'm not good with my hands, so sewing is hard for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '있다'의 반대로, 손으로 하는 일이 서툰 사람에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 있다, for someone clumsy with handwork.

phrases.en: He is very skilled with his hands and even makes furniture.
phrases.nuance_ko: '좋다'보다 더 크게 칭찬하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A stronger compliment than 좋다.
phrases.en_equiv: to be highly skilled with one's hands

explain_en: You say '손재주가 있다/없다' or '좋다/뛰어나다', and it isn't used for verbal skill or intelligence. The similar '손끝이 야무지다' praises neat, careful work, and skill in cooking is called '손맛' instead.

en: to be careful; to be prudent

examples.en: He is a man of few words and careful.
You have to make big decisions carefully.
She is careful by nature, so she rarely makes mistakes.
Right now you need to be more careful.
He is careful, so his decisions are a bit slow.
I'm sorry I spoke without thinking.

explain: 신중하다는 행동하기 전에 깊이 생각하고 조심하는 모습이에요. '조심하다'는 위험이나 실수를 피하려고 주의하는 것이고, 신중하다는 결정이나 말을 가볍게 하지 않는다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 반대말은 '경솔하다'예요.

phrases.en: He is a person who is careful in his words and actions.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신중하다'를 '신중한'으로 바꿔 사람의 성격을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form 신중한 describes a person's character.

phrases.en: Please think carefully before you decide.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신중하게'는 동사 앞에 붙어 행동하는 방식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 신중하게 goes before a verb to describe how something is done.

phrases.en: Saying it like that is not careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 행동이 가볍다고 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say gently that words or actions are careless.

explain_en: Thinking carefully before deciding or acting; neutral, a trait. 신중하다 describes thinking deeply and taking care before acting. '조심하다' is watching out to avoid danger or mistakes, while 신중하다 stresses not deciding or speaking lightly. The opposite is '경솔하다'.

t90.ax: I'm sorry I spoke without thinking.

examples.ko: 동생은 준비성이 좋아서 늘 우산을 들고 다녀요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is well-prepared and always carries an umbrella.

examples.ko: 준비성이 철저한 친구 덕분에 여행이 편했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my thorough, well-prepared friend, the trip was easy.

examples.ko: 준비성 없이 나왔다가 비를 홀딱 맞았어요.
examples.en: I came out unprepared and got completely soaked in the rain.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 준비성이 부족해서 항상 마지막에 서둘러요.
examples.en: He lacks preparedness, so he always rushes at the end.
Everyone was amazed at our team leader's preparedness.
Preparedness starts from small habits.

explain: '준비'는 하는 일이고 '준비성'은 미리 챙기는 성격이에요. '준비성이 있다/없다/철저하다'처럼 사람의 성격을 말할 때 쓰고, '-성'이 성질을 나타내는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 준비성이 있어서 늘 믿음이 가요.
phrases.en: That friend is well prepared, so I can always trust them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 챙기는 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone who plans ahead.

phrases.example: 저는 준비성이 없어서 자주 우산을 놓고 와요.
phrases.en: I'm not very prepared, so I often forget my umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 챙기지 않는 성격을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe someone who does not plan ahead.

phrases.example: 준비성이 철저해서 짐을 하루 전에 다 쌌어요.
phrases.en: I'm very thorough about preparing, so I packed everything a day before.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 꼼꼼하게 챙기는 정도가 아주 높을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone prepares ahead very carefully and thoroughly.

explain_en: '준비' is the act of preparing, while '준비성' is the trait of getting ready ahead of time. It is used for a person's character, as in '준비성이 있다/없다/철저하다', where '-성' marks a quality.

examples.en: This is a pristine area, so the air is clean.
This is seafood raised in pristine waters.
We have to protect Jeju Island's pristine nature.

examples.ko: 청정 에너지를 쓰는 차가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of cars that run on clean energy is growing.
We swam in a pristine mountain valley stream.
It is a fish that lives only in unpolluted water.

explain: 보통 '청정 지역', '청정 에너지'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여서 써요. 사람 손이 닿지 않은 깨끗함이라서, 방이나 옷이 깨끗하다고 할 때는 '깨끗하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 우리나라는 청정 에너지를 더 늘리고 있어요.
phrases.en: Our country is increasing its use of clean energy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경을 해치지 않는 에너지를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Energy that doesn't harm the environment.

phrases.example: 청정 자연 속에서 며칠 쉬고 왔어요.
phrases.en: I rested for a few days in unspoiled nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 손이 닿지 않은 깨끗한 자연을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Clean nature that people have barely touched.

phrases.en: I turned on the air purifier in the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '청정'이 들어간 가장 흔한 생활 용품 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common everyday item whose name contains '청정'.

explain_en: It usually sits in front of another noun, as in '청정 지역' and '청정 에너지'. It means purity untouched by people, so for a clean room or clean clothes you say '깨끗하다' instead.

examples.en: Housekeepers often appear in old dramas.

examples.ko: 그 부잣집에는 가정부 두 명이 일해요.
examples.en: Two housekeepers work in that wealthy household.
I saw an advertisement looking for a housekeeper.

examples.ko: 영화 속 가정부는 사실 비밀을 알고 있었어요.
examples.en: The housekeeper in the movie actually knew a secret.
A housekeeper who came from abroad helps with the housework.
Thanks to the housekeeper, the house is always clean.

explain: 요즘 일상에서는 '가정부'보다 '가사도우미', '도우미 아주머니'라고 더 많이 말해요. 가정부는 드라마나 영화에서 자주 들리는 오래된 느낌의 말이에요. 직접 부를 때는 '이모님'처럼 존중하는 호칭을 써요.

phrases.en: A housekeeper comes to our house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 같은 뜻의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The more common modern word for the same job.

phrases.en: That family lives with a housekeeper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집안일을 맡길 사람을 두는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a household keeps someone for housework.

phrases.en: Auntie, please take care of dinner tonight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부를 때 쓰는 존중하는 호칭이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful form of address when calling the person directly.

explain_en: Hired housekeeper — paid helper who works in someone else's home. In daily life people now more often say 가사도우미 or 도우미 아주머니 than 가정부. 가정부 sounds a bit old-fashioned and shows up mostly in dramas and movies. When speaking to the person directly, a respectful title like 이모님 is used.
